caption: The drawing depicts a single large jug or pitcher, which is central and vertically oriented on a plain, cream-colored background. The jug has a bulbous, textured body that is primarily blue with subtle, irregular lighter blue-gray patterns resembling marbling or stoneware glaze, and it is banded by two horizontal gray metallic rings, one at the rim and one at the base of the body. The pitcher’s neck, flared spout, lid, and handle are gray and have a metallic sheen, with the lid fitting over the top and the handle being ornate and elongated, curving from the body to the top. The base of the pitcher is flat and brown, indicating it may be wood or another material distinct from the rest of the vessel. The background is mostly empty, except for some light discolorations and blemishes. The artist's signature, "Helen Bronson," appears in small letters near the lower right side of the drawing.
title: Pewter and Ceramic Pitcher
